name: Congenital Trigeminal Anesthesia

criteria.description: Congenital absence or severe reduction of facial pain and temperature sensation in trigeminal nerve distribution
Preserved motor function of trigeminal nerve including masticatory muscles
Exclusion of acquired causes such as trauma, infection, or neoplasm affecting trigeminal nerve
Neurophysiological studies showing absent or diminished trigeminal sensory nerve action potentials
Normal brain MRI excluding structural lesions of trigeminal pathways

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: All three major criteria must be met for diagnosis
diagnosticCriteria.notes: Diagnosis is clinical and supported by neurophysiology and imaging to exclude other causes.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Congenital loss of pain and temperature sensation in trigeminal nerve distribution
searchTerms: born without pain and temperature feeling on face

pathognomonic.symptomName: Absence of corneal reflex due to trigeminal sensory deficit
searchTerms: no blink reflex due to facial numbness

common.symptomName: Recurrent facial injuries due to lack of protective sensation
searchTerms: repeated facial wounds due to no pain

common.symptomName: Mild facial anesthesia with preserved touch sensation
searchTerms: mild facial numbness but normal touch
reduced pain but normal touch feeling

common.symptomName: Impaired corneal healing secondary to absent sensation
searchTerms: slow eye healing due to no sensation

occasional.notes: Due to lack of pain perception

occasional.symptomName: Mild facial asymmetry from repeated trauma
searchTerms: slight unevenness of face from trauma
face shape changes from repeated injury

occasional.symptomName: Dry eye symptoms due to impaired blink reflex
searchTerms: impaired eye moisture due to blink reflex

occasional.symptomName: Occasional headaches related to trigeminal dysfunction

rare.symptomName: Trigeminal trophic syndrome with facial ulceration
searchTerms: facial skin ulcers from nerve damage

rare.symptomName: Secondary corneal ulceration leading to vision loss
searchTerms: eye surface ulcer leading to poor sight

rare.symptomName: Mild developmental delay due to repeated infections

imaging: Normal brain MRI excluding structural lesions of trigeminal nerve or brainstem
genetic: Rare familial cases suggest possible genetic etiology though specific genes not well defined
other: Absent or diminished trigeminal sensory nerve action potentials on neurophysiological testing

redFlags: Sudden onset of facial anesthesia suggesting acquired cause
Presence of facial rash or vesicles
Progressive neurological deficits beyond trigeminal distribution
references: Dyck PJ, et al. Congenital trigeminal anesthesia: clinical and neurophysiological features. Neurology. 1980.
Bannister LH, et al. Disorders of the trigeminal nerve. In: Neurology and Clinical Neuroscience. 2015.
